dedupe_keys.name: epa enviroatlas meter scale urban land cover mulc

description: MULC is a one-metre resolution land cover dataset for 30 US communities, produced for the EPA EnviroAtlas. It classifies the landscape into impervious surface, tree, grass and herbaceous, shrub, soil and barren, water, wetland and agriculture, using several classification methods on aerial photography and LiDAR, with a mean overall fuzzy accuracy of 88% and a mean Kappa of 0.84 across communities. MULC underlies about 100 EnviroAtlas metrics on ecosystem goods and services. It was produced by the EPA Office of Research and Development and is accessible free in the EnviroAtlas web browser, as a web map service in GIS, and as downloadable data from the EPA Environmental Data Gateway, with fact sheets and metadata per community; a 2020 Remote Sensing paper by Pilant and others gives class definitions and guidance. Caveats: coverage is limited to selected communities, imagery dates differ between communities, and development of the dataset is ongoing. It supports mapping of green and grey infrastructure, street tree planting, urban heat island analysis and stormwater runoff modelling; a related record is i-Tree.
